status: DOCUMENT_ONLY; comparison applicability and physical qualification UNKNOWN

requirements.existing_contract: Mission construction selects source/stations/targets and planned leg geometry. planCycle returns a deterministic prescribed quasi-static plan at its inputs. The served selector keys source hashes/import stamp, class, distance, wind, requested mode, CFG and candidate set; selected record-basis options and proof are retained, with favourable output separately labelled. Its audit compares inputs, basis, mode, config/model and replay outputs. These predicates are model checks, not physical qualification.
prospective_record_requirements: Exact source revision and hashes/import identity, route/source/target geometry, class/mode/options, all configuration and wind-input provenance, plan state/reason, record or favourable basis, selected proof and output record; each consumer identified
requirements.insufficient_or_disconfirming_evidence: A matching class name or drawn scene cannot establish matching inputs, selected controls, basis or physical completion. A standby/unavailable selection cannot be silently compared as a ready cycle.

requirements.existing_contract: The host stores simTime, pause/speed and lastFrame. Frame timestamp differences are divided to seconds and capped before speed multiplication; pause holds model time. UI phase stepping changes simTime. Dead battery state freezes the stateAt input at deadAt. Model T+ is not UTC, uninterrupted wall time or a measured flight clock.
prospective_record_requirements: Raw clock type, epoch/origin, units, timestamps and acquisition metadata; pause/speed/clamp and phase-step events, deadAt/frozen-state flags and actual model-time record; separate raw-clock-to-model-time alignment and calibration record
requirements.insufficient_or_disconfirming_evidence: A screenshot or common elapsed label cannot identify the clock, origin, paused/jumped interval or freeze. No raw-clock alignment can be inferred from displayed T+.

requirements.existing_contract: Plan durations and cycleMin use minutes; mission cycleSec and cumulative phaseEnds use seconds. stateAt adds the mission offset, wraps the input and chooses the first end strictly above wrapped time, then local progress. Cycle number also addresses rotating targets/stations. Served binding rebuilds these bounds or clears them when unavailable. The analysis generator accumulates phase durations from the source-cycle origin, without the host mission offset.
prospective_record_requirements: Model time origin and raw input, offset, cycle number, selected station/target and phase ID/order, phase bounds/progress, secondsIntoPhase/cycleMinute and exact plan identity; state transition and inactive flags
requirements.insufficient_or_disconfirming_evidence: Same phase name or cycle-minute value across records cannot establish same cycle, offset, target, station or phase duration. Analysis-cycle time is not automatically the host display clock.

requirements.existing_contract: cycleLimits includes verdict-mesh points, extrema refinement and explicit one-sided seam samples; the printed phase generator refines a phase peak and retains its signed value, progress, local seconds, cycle minute and limits. JSON rows are summaries of failing phases on prescribed inputs, not a chronological observed trajectory. A phase with no printed failing peak is not evidence of physical completion.
prospective_record_requirements: Exact phase and seam identifier, left/right/interior/endpoint convention, ordered sample timestamps, sampling/refinement provenance and original unrounded result; raw observed series kept distinct from model extrema and summary records
requirements.insufficient_or_disconfirming_evidence: Matching rounded time or a phase peak does not establish identical seam side, chronological response, neighbouring state or observational coverage. Do not reconstruct a trajectory from phase maxima.

requirements.existing_contract: Signed unheldT is an authority residual: positive unsupported surplus lift, negative unavailable upward authority. Its owners include bag, rotor, aerodynamic and vertical-drag terms. stateAt netN omits those actuator/aerodynamic/drag owners and is a different quantity; it must not be relabelled unheld force. Host inventory tonnes, power MW and ground speed km/h are mapped into visual fractions and speed m/s. Adapter airspeed and groundSpeed currently both read host gs, while verticalSpeed uses phaseShape; channel names do not establish measured air-relative speed or observed vertical motion.
prospective_record_requirements: Quantity definition and owner boundary, sign/direction, original unit and conversion source, supplied/fallback/default status, actual input fields and calibration/uncertainty; retain each original residual/limit and no new conversion
requirements.insufficient_or_disconfirming_evidence: Absolute magnitude, netN, visual speed labels or silently defaulted values cannot replace signed residuals, original units or an observed channel. Missing telemetry is not zero.

requirements.existing_contract: trackBearing declares degrees from north for the route; stateAt instead uses bezBearing/atan2 radians for the drawn geographic heading. Positive model vertical speed follows increasing prescribed altitude. Local model vectors use nose-forward x, port-positive y and up-positive z, with origin at hull centre of buoyancy. Heights in config use hull-centre relative to source water/reference ground; the terrain reference bridges the atmosphere ledger. The published geometric/MSL versus geopotential-height disagreement and constant mismatch remain an open MISS, not reconciled by this map.
prospective_record_requirements: Geographic datum and lon/lat order, bearing units/reference, local/body/world frame and origin, transform provenance, reference water/terrain height and geometric/geopotential definition, sensor calibration and uncertainty
units_or_conventions: route degrees versus state heading radians from north
requirements.insufficient_or_disconfirming_evidence: An altitudeM label, common numeric height, phaseShape visual attitude or shared constants cannot establish compatible frames, altitude datums or atmospheric inputs. Preserve conflicting source contracts until explicitly resolved.
requirements.prospective_custodian_role: Coordinate, height-datum and calibration provenance custodian

requirements.existing_contract: Host six-phase state and standalone eleven-phase demonstration remain distinct. The adapter passes recognised phases, maps absent/unknown off-cycle phases to WEATHER_HOLD, overlaps hose progress and converts inventory to fill fractions; host alt takes precedence but phaseShape supplies other channels. Shared constants do not make the timelines or illustrative power shares identical. Visual defaults and supplied/fallback fields are not measurements.
prospective_record_requirements: Consumer/module and host-versus-standalone identity, original phase and transformed phase, field-by-field supplied/fallback/null/default provenance, original host state and view state, mapping revision, declaration of inactive/off-cycle status and applicable record scope
requirements.insufficient_or_disconfirming_evidence: An equivalent drawing or matching phase label cannot demonstrate same prescribed state, output history or physical observation. Off-cycle fallback must not hide the original state/reason.

requirements.existing_contract: No raw measured time series, clock calibration, synchronization or acquisition uncertainty is supplied by this paper. Prescribed values and source extrema remain existing model records. Alignment of future instruments to each other and to an event reference is separate from any mapping to prescribed model elapsed time.
prospective_record_requirements: Unaltered raw acquisition timestamps and declared clock/epoch/unit, responsible calibration/synchronization evidence, event marker definitions, drift/latency and uncertainty provenance, explicit alignment transformation/version and data gaps; separately justified comparison applicability, matched inputs, frame and phase/seam address
units_or_conventions: s only where source declares seconds
requirements.insufficient_or_disconfirming_evidence: Uncalibrated timestamp coincidence, resampled curves, guessed epoch or a model duration cannot supply missing measured-clock evidence or a new physical acceptance rule. No threshold or alignment calculation is selected.

* TERRAIN_MSL — one reference elevation for the ground the fleet works over. An assumption,
 * and a deliberately coarse one: the southern interior plateau runs about 900–1,400 m, and
 * the model carries a single figure for the lake and the fire alike rather than pretending
 * to know the ground under each. A ship recovering onto a valley floor is lower and needs
 * more ballast to reach it; that limit is stated with the nitrogen tankage below.
 *
 * WORK_ALT_MSL — the ceiling of ALT.cruise over that plateau. It is the WORST case in the
 * cycle: every other point a ship reaches is lower, in denser air, with more lift. Sizing
 * here therefore sizes for everywhere.
 *
 * THE TERRAIN ENVELOPE, because "1,500 m above ground" is a profile, not a clearance claim.
 * The fires that matter in the interior burn between the valley floors — Okanagan and
 * Thompson, 300–500 m — and treeline, about 2,100 m in the southern interior. Local summits
 * inside that fuel belt reach roughly 2,320 m at Big White. A 2,500 m MSL ceiling clears the
 * fuel everywhere in the belt and the highest ground in it by about 180 m. Flying lower was
 * permitted as relief from the hull growth below and is not taken: it buys a smaller
 * envelope by putting the largest aircraft ever proposed under the ridgelines it is working.
 */
export const TERRAIN_MSL = 1000;                       // m, interior plateau reference
export const WORK_ALT_MSL = TERRAIN_MSL + ALT.cruise;  // m, 2,500 — where the hulls are sized

## 18. Three atmosphere implementations that do not agree to the last digit

Tracking issue: [#16](https://github.com/PinkRobotics/airships/issues/16).

**Reproduced 2026-10-01. Open.** Run `make labelledcheck` and read the density rows at 1,000 m in
`research/validation/report.md`. `sim/atmosphere.js` returns 1.111642738880746 kg/m³;
`research/analysis/vacuum-cell.py` and `research/analysis/helium.py` both return
1.111652281952491 kg/m³; Table I of the 1976 standard prints 1.1116. With the tolerance written
before the first run (0.00005 kg/m³) the browser model agrees, and the two Python copies MISS by
about 0.0000023 kg/m³ beyond it.

The cause is the gas constant for dry air: `sim/atmosphere.js` uses 287.0528 J/(kg·K) and the two
Python files use 287.05. All three also treat their argument as geopotential height, although the
JavaScript interface describes it as height above mean sea level: at a geometric 2,500 m the
standard's temperature is 271.906 K against the functions' 271.900 K.

It stays a MISS. The constant feeds the cell parity mirror and the generated analysis figures, so
it is not changed quietly. Decide the altitude contract and the constant together, publish what
moves, old and new, then move the row.
